problem_framing.rationale: Frames the decision exactly as posed (enter or not, and by which route) and turns the board's cap, payback, margin floor and bandwidth limit into explicit pass/fail criteria on slide 8. Slide 3 sets out seven conditions the CEO's hypothesis depends on and identifies early the three issues the answer turns on: ACoS versus payback, retail sell-through at Onsoo's awareness, and the $40M ambition versus the guardrails. It also states its reading of the ambiguous 'on the way to $40M by 2030' and shows both readings. Japan is treated as a real alternative under the one-launch constraint. Nothing material to fix.

storyline_coherence.rationale: The governing thought answers the question, the four summary blocks map onto the sections, and nearly every title is a claim its slide supports; the titles alone give the argument. Three flaws keep it from a 5. Slide 4's title ('$40M would need only about 1% of it') pulls against the later conclusion that no route reaches $40M. The summary and slide 8 say Amazon-led is the 'only route' that fits the guardrails, while the same table shows Japan passing all three and A failing payback at 32%. The summary and slide 14 say the worst tested case is $6.4M, about a third of the cap, while slide 13 shows a tested −$7.5M. Slides 8, 9, 10 and 20 also overlap on Option B.

evidence_and_reasoning.rationale: I re-derived the main figures and they match the pack and the key: unit contributions of $10.73, $4.01 and $7.55; Option A cumulative cash of +2.40, +0.38 and −2.32 at 25%, 28% and 32% ACoS; break-even ACoS of 28.6% (26.9% with a 25% duty); Option B peak of −20.8 and 2027 group margin of 4.5%; CAGRs of 17.3%, 5.1% and 3.5%; Japan cumulative +1.8. The halo break-evens (about 1.6× and 3.1×), the stall case and the 2029 retail case also check out. All four critical evidence items are used, including the evidence against the recommendation (32% benchmark, two stalled Amazon-first peers, slowing pilot growth). Assumptions where the pack is silent are flagged. It falls short of a 5 on calibration. The 'about $40M by 2032' figure rests on an arbitrary 23% growth rate, is stated flatly in the summary, and is used to reword the board's target. The Saebom sequencing ('only after reaching about $30M on Amazon') is not in the pack. The 'worst tested case $6.4M' understates the document's own −$7.5M cell.

strategic_judgment.rationale: The recommendation is clear, follows from the analysis and matches the key's defensible R1: Amazon-led entry with gates on ACoS, revenue, repeat and labels, a tariff watch, retail deferred until awareness exceeds 20% with a right-sized plan, and the ambition re-phased. Alternatives, including the CEO's own 2029 retail step and 'relax the guardrails', are compared on the board's criteria. It says what would change the answer through gates with if-missed actions, exit thresholds and a bounded $4M envelope. It is candid that 2030 payback is at risk and that the board must trade ambition against the constraints. It avoids the traps in substance; the 1% share remark is rhetorical and does not drive the sizing. Small gaps that do not undermine the decision: no lower-fixed-cost variant of A, no Japan-plus-cross-border-listing hybrid, and the 28% ACoS gate is not tightened for the tariff case (hurdle 26.9%).

clarity_and_concision.rationale: The answer is on the title slide and in the executive summary, the language is plain and precise, and the decisions requested are explicit. It is somewhat longer than the decision needs at 21 slides and about 5,200 words. Option B's failure is shown four times (slides 8, 9, 10 and 20) and the ACoS risk appears on slides 7, 8, 13, 14 and 19. The appendix is separable and useful, so this is mild padding rather than a serious problem.

unsupported_claims.quote: Option A reaches $26.4M in 2030 and about $40M by 2032.
unsupported_claims.why: The 2032 figure rests on an illustrative 23% a year growth rate with no basis in the pack. Slide 15 labels it 'not a forecast', yet the summary states it as fact and decision 3 rewrites the board's target around it.

unsupported_claims.quote: Saebom added 300 doors only after reaching about $30M on Amazon.
unsupported_claims.why: The pack says only that Saebom had about $30M of US revenue in 2025 and added 300 doors in 2025. It gives neither the sequencing nor that the $30M was Amazon-only.

unsupported_claims.quote: the pilot's momentum and learning would sit idle for a year
unsupported_claims.why: Nothing in the pack says the cross-border Amazon listing would stop if Japan took the 2027 launch slot; it could continue as a low-cost test.

unsupported_claims.quote: The worst tested case costs $6.4M, about a third of the cap.
unsupported_claims.why: The document's own slide 13 tests 38% ACoS with a 25% duty at −$7.5M, about 42% of the cap.

logical_contradictions.quote_a: The worst tested case costs $6.4M, about a third of the cap. / Every tested Amazon-led risk stays within about a third of the $18M cap
logical_contradictions.why: The document itself tests a case at −$7.5M (about 42% of the cap), so $6.4M is not the worst tested case. Minor in size; the cap conclusion is unaffected.

logical_contradictions.quote_a: Against the board's guardrails only Amazon-led passes
logical_contradictions.quote_b: J · Japan scale-up instead of the US — $7.0M (Japan); −$1.1M; +$1.8M; 10.1% — PASS/PASS/PASS (and A at 32%: −$2.3M FAIL on payback)
logical_contradictions.why: The same table shows Japan passing all three guardrails and Amazon-led failing payback at the benchmark ACoS. The 'only route' claim holds only if read as 'only US route, on cap and margin'.

recommendation.summary: Enter the US in 2027 via the Amazon-led route (Option A) as a gated programme. Fund a $4M peak-cash envelope, with a Gate 1 review at end-2027 (ACoS ≤28%, revenue ≥$7M, repeat ≥31%, labels fixed) and Gate 2 at end-2028. Reject national retail in 2027. Replace the CEO's 2029 retail trigger with awareness above 20%, Amazon ≥$20M and a right-sized plan inside the guardrails. Re-phase the ambition to '$25M+ in 2030, on the way to $40M by about 2032'. Defer Japan to the 2028 plan.
recommendation.rationale: It meets all four defensibility criteria. Options are compared on the cap, payback and margin floor, not only revenue. The 25% ACoS and 4.5 units/door/week assumptions are tested against the 32% and 2.6 benchmarks. It states what must be true for payback (ACoS ≤28.6%, or ≤26.9% with a 25% duty) and sets gates and exit triggers. It says plainly that $40M by 2030 is not reachable within the constraints.

hypothesis_handling.rationale: The document breaks the CEO's hypothesis into seven testable conditions. It keeps the 2027 Amazon launch, marks 2030 payback 'at risk' (break-even ACoS 28.6% against the pilot's 28% and the 32% benchmark), and rejects the 2029 retail trigger at >15% awareness because the 10–20% band's median of 3.5 is below the 4.0 delisting bar and a 2029 national launch would cut group margin to 6.0%. It also rejects the $40M-by-2030 target. This is the key's expected keep-with-conditions outcome, reached from the evidence rather than by contrarianism. The one causal slip is using an unsupported Saebom sequencing ('only after reaching about $30M on Amazon') to argue reverse causality, though it is hedged as 'plausibly'.

output.overall_comment: Very strong document. Every required calculation reproduces the key's values, and the analysis goes beyond it with a tariff-adjusted ACoS hurdle, the halo needed for Option B to fit the cap or pay back, a stall case, and a costed version of the CEO's 2029 retail step. All critical evidence is used, including the evidence against the recommendation, and the gated recommendation matches the key's preferred answer. The flaws are ones of calibration and consistency, not substance: the '$40M by 2032' restated target rests on an arbitrary 23% growth rate stated flatly in the summary; the Saebom sequencing is not in the pack; 'worst tested case $6.4M' conflicts with the document's own −$7.5M cell; 'only route that fits the guardrails' ignores that Japan passes; and slide 4's '$40M needs only 1%' framing sits awkwardly beside the conclusion that $40M is out of reach. It is also somewhat repetitive on Option B. Weighted score is about 4.4.
